subject: Orbit Exchange - Gen API latency spike & mitigation

Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] gen-api p99 jump for orbit-exchange (region: us-west)

Heads-up — our gen-api p99 for Orbit Exchange (customer: Orbit Exchange, prod cluster us-west) jumped to ~4.1s at 07:09 PDT. Baseline p99 is typically ~0.6s.

Quick facts:
- Spike start: ~07:08 PDT
- Recent traffic: 2.1k rps (bursting from a scheduled batch); sustained 60s window shows larger seq lengths
- Initial probe: several nodes reporting elevated kernel scheduling + KV cache misses

I'm spinning up a quick perf dump and attaching p99 graphs (stub). Will follow with a short timeline.

Attachments: p99_latency_graphs.png (image stub)

Ben
SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p99 jump for orbit-exchange (region: us-west)

On Mon, Sep 5, 2027 at 7:12 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Heads-up — our gen-api p99 for Orbit Exchange...

Triage started. Early hypothesis: KV cache evaporation + heavy long-sequence requests from a new client batch.
Immediate actions I'm taking now:
- Routing rule: move Orbit Exchange traffic to fallback pool with larger KV cache budgets (5–10m window) — in flight
- Canary rollback: prepping a quick rollback to the previous routing policy if fallbacks don't reduce p99 <= 800ms in next 15m
- Informing Jordan so we can prepare a short customer note (what we did / next steps)

Marking this P1. If routing change fails, we escalate to infra and propose throttles or short-term q8 quantized variant for heavy customers.

Marissa
Director, Product Ops (serving)
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 07:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p99 jump for orbit-exchange (region: us-west)

Marissa / Ben — quick update from runtime team:
- Root-cause (prelim): mismatch in cache eviction thresholds after last rolling update; some nodes dropped hot KV entries prematurely under long-seq bursts.
- Evidence: cache-miss counters + elevated kernel wait on 3/12 hosting nodes (see attached heap snapshot, metrics slices).

Planned mitigation (ETA ~20m):
1) Apply routing change to shift 30% of Orbit traffic to an isolated fallback pool (already kicked by Marissa).
2) Deploy a small patch to reset eviction thresholds and prefill KV for the next 30m window.
3) If p99 > 1.2s after 25m, enable temporary quantized variant (q8) for Orbit to reduce token CPU and improve latency — this reduces quality by a small margin but keeps SLAs.

I attached a short incident timeline spreadsheet (incident_timeline_20270905.xlsx) and a table of node-level metrics.

Dylan
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: DRAFT: Orbit Exchange incident note — please review before I send to customer

Team — drafting the customer note, please review and flag any inaccurate technical points or asks for the roadmap. I want to send within 30 minutes.

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE (for Orbit Exchange) ---
Subject: Brief outage note: elevated latency on Redwood Gen API (Sep 5)

Sam / Claire —

We observed elevated latency on requests served to your account earlier today (Sep 5). Our team identified a cache eviction regression affecting a subset of serving nodes which caused higher-than-normal p99 values for some requests.

What we did:
- Immediately shifted your traffic to a fallback pool with increased cache budgets.
- Deployed a configuration patch to stabilize eviction thresholds.
- Prepared a short incident timeline and graphs (attached).

Impact: transient latency spikes (p99 peaked ~4.1s); the bulk of requests remained within SLA after the fallback rules.

Next steps and asks we expect from product/roadmap:
- Short-term: we recommend allowing temporary routing to fallback pool for recurring batch windows — requires Ops approval to add an exception rule in routing policies.
- Mid-term (roadmap ask): add per-customer cache budget tuning and automated prefill logic for predictable batch windows.
- Please let us know if you want us to enable a temporary lower-cost q8 model variant while we harden caching behavior.

Would appreciate any wording edits before I send.

--- end draft ---

Notes: Marissa, can you confirm the rollback plan and whether we need a formal SLA exception ticket? Dylan — confirm that q8 toggle is safe from a quality/regressions perspective and approximate time to flip. Ben — add any missing monitoring links.

Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 5 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Orbit Exchange — brief update: elevated latency earlier today (resolved)

Sam / Claire —

Quick update from the Redwood team on the elevated latency you saw this morning:

What happened: a regression in cache eviction thresholds during a rolling update caused higher-than-normal p99 for a subset of requests to your account.
What we did: we shifted your traffic to a fallback pool and deployed a config patch to stabilize eviction behavior. We monitored the cluster for 45 minutes and validated p99 returned to expected levels.
Impact: peak p99 ~4.1s for a short window; most traffic remained within SLA after the fallback.
Attachments: p99_latency_graphs.png; incident_timeline_20270905.xlsx (both attached).

Recommended next steps (we'd like your permission to proceed):
- Temporary routing exception: allow fallback pool routing for scheduled batch windows (Ops change; reduces risk of repeat incidents).
- Roadmap ask (for your visibility): we are prioritizing per-customer cache budgets and automated prefill; rough ETA Q4.
- Optional: we can enable a temporary quantized variant (q8) during your highest-volume windows as a protective measure; this trades off minor output quality for steady latency.

If you'd like a short 15-minute sync to walk through the timeline and mitigations, I'm available at 09:30 or 10:30 PDT today.

Thanks — and apologies for the disruption. We're following up with a post-incident note and next steps.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability
